newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel says ready to sell 74 pct of KIOCL.
newsitem.headline: India panel says ready to sell 74 pct of KIOCL.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission said on Friday it was prepared to sell 74 percent of state-run iron ore producer Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Ltd (KIOCL) if a suitable strategic partner emerged.

"There is an urgent need for strengthening the management of the company," the commission, appointed last year to recommend a partial privatisation strategy, said in a report presented to the government on Thursday.

Major decisions needed to be taken to ensure the future viability of the company, it said. "The commission feels that this would be the opportune time for inducting a strategic partner into the company," it said.
The government has already sold 1.0 percent of KIOCL, which has an equity of 6.34 billion rupees.
"The strategic partner may be offered 30 percent of equity to start with and also (be) inducted in the management of the company," the report said.
"The government may also enter into an agreement with the strategic partner providing for a further dilution of government equity to the extent of 43 percent within two years," it said.

This could be done through a combination of a further offer of equity shares of 10 percent to the strategic partner and a public offer of the balance to the domestic institutional investors and retail investors, it said.
The phased disinvestment would leave the government with a 26 percent stake of the equity, it said.
KIOCL earned net profit of 950 million rupees ($26.5 million) in 1995/96 (April-March), compared with 576 million rupees in 1994/95. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
